name: Internal CRUD tool
description: A back-office tool used by employees to create, read, update and delete operational records.

controls.rationale: The tool exists to create, read, update and delete records that must survive restarts, so a real persistence lifecycle is mandatory.
Internal tools still need to restrict who can view or change records, even behind a corporate network boundary.
Users are a known, internal employee population; the team has not committed to a public accessibility budget for this tool.

architectureChoices.rationale: Employees already have corporate accounts; reusing SSO avoids standing up a second credential store.
CRUD-heavy workflows are fastest as data-dense tables rather than one-record-per-page forms.

clarificationQuestions.prompt: คาดว่าจะมีจำนวน record กี่รายการในปีแรก?
clarificationQuestions.whyItMatters: ปริมาณ record กำหนดว่าต้องมี pagination/indexing ตั้งแต่ต้น หรือ query ตรง ๆ ก็เพียงพอ

clarificationQuestions.prompt: ต้องเก็บ audit log ว่าใครแก้ record ไหนเมื่อไรไหม?
clarificationQuestions.whyItMatters: ถ้าต้องมี audit trail ต้องออกแบบ schema แยกตั้งแต่ต้น ผูกเพิ่มทีหลังต้อง backfill ย้อนหลังซึ่งทำยาก

performance.rationale: Employees on a corporate network open this tool deliberately and keep it open, so the cost of a slower first load is far lower than on a public site.
Data-dense admin tables are allowed to take longer to parse than a content page, but not so long that the tool feels broken on a first visit.

accessibility.rationale: A known employee audience is not a reason to ship a page somebody on the team cannot use at all; serious and critical findings stay disallowed even where the control itself is optional.
Minor and moderate findings are tolerated for an internal tool with a known audience, which is the difference this profile exists to express; the ceiling stops that tolerance from becoming unlimited.
